about: What Year Is It? shows Robin Williams as Alan Parrish in Jumanji (1995), just after he has escaped from the jungle inside the board game. He has wild long hair, a scraggly beard and a leaf-and-hide outfit, and he is staring at the camera with confused, startled eyes. In the film he has been trapped for 26 years, so his first question on returning is what year it is. Online the frame stands for anyone who has been cut off from the world for a while, whether that is waking from a long nap, finishing exams or coming back from a camping trip with no signal.
origin: Jumanji came out in December 1995 with Robin Williams as Alan, who is pulled into the game as a boy and released decades later as a grown man. The confused "what year is it?" reaction was used widely in rage comics and reaction-image threads.
usage:
The top box is usually the situation that cut you off: a three-hour nap, finals week, a long flight, a binge of a 10-season show. Often it is left empty. The bottom box is the question itself, "what year is it?", or a related panicked question.

It works best when the absence was shorter than it feels. A nap that was meant to be 20 minutes, a weekend offline, returning to a game after one patch, or opening a group chat with 900 unread messages are all perfect. Keep the top line short so Alan's bewildered face carries the joke.
ideas: waking up from a 20 minute nap at 9 pm
opening the group chat after a weekend off
logging back into the game after one patch
aka: Robin Williams What Year Is It
